title: What If Every Squirrel Vanished? Your Forest Would Notice

scenes.text: What if every squirrel vanished? Your local forest would lose its busiest gardener.
A fox squirrel hides roughly 3,000 to 10,000 nuts a year, each in its own spot.
In one estimate, as many as 74 percent of buried nuts are never dug up again.
Those forgotten nuts can sprout. Squirrels bury red oak acorns, which stay dormant until spring.
In one model, seven times as many black walnuts sprouted when gray squirrels gathered them than when red squirrels did.
Oaks would not vanish overnight, since blue jays bury acorns too. But the planting crew would shrink.

description:
What if every squirrel vanished?
They bury thousands of nuts a year and forget many of them, which helps forests regrow.
